title: State Hermitage Museum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Handclasps, embraces, glances and gaps organise relationships across twenty selected works.
introduction:
In Matisse's *Dance*, a gap between reaching hands keeps the ring from becoming a finished pattern. In *Music*, separate bodies belong together without touching at all. The two paintings offer a particularly clear comparison of how a group can be constructed. Earlier works in this selection make relationships through subtler means: an infant reaching for a book, a woman extending her hand towards unseen light, or a child looking out from an embrace.

Follow these connections before treating a picture as a set of individual figures. The spaces between bodies can be as consequential as their expressions. This approach also makes comparison possible across styles without pretending that resemblance establishes direct influence.
visitNote: The Hermitage collection occupies several buildings, and modern European paintings are associated with the General Staff Building. This is a collection selection, not a route through one palace. Check individual works for current location and loans. The monochrome reproduction of Zorah Standing cannot convey its painted colours.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: Leonardo’s notes on gesture, light and the body provide questions to bring to the earlier paintings here. Compare those concerns with the much more reduced bodies of Matisse, without treating the book as an explanation for every work.

works.title: Danaë
works.credit: Rembrandt van Rijn. Danae. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The extended hand reaches towards light rather than a fully depicted visitor. Rembrandt gives the mythological encounter a visible expectation while leaving its other participant outside the immediate scene. Heavy curtains enclose the bed, but the turning body opens that enclosure. The relationship is established through response, before the cause of the response has been completely shown.

works.title: The Lute Player
works.credit: Caravaggio. The Lute Player. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The open score, flowers and fruit occupy the near space before the musician. Caravaggio gives the performance a material setting, with music, food and growing things sharing the same limited space. The lute's rounded form and bright shirt bring the player close, while the objects retain separate claims on attention. The picture assembles a moment whose elements will not all last equally long.

works.title: Dance II
works.credit: Henri Matisse. Dance (II). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-matisse/dance-ii-1910
works.description: Five figures make a ring, but the reaching hands leave a visible interruption. That gap turns connection into an effort still being made. Matisse reduces the setting to green ground and blue sky, so the red-orange bodies carry the action without a surrounding story. The circle remains dynamic because its closure is not completely secure.

works.title: Music
works.credit: Music. WikiArt; Henri Matisse. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Open intervals separate the figures. Repeated red bodies and measured spacing establish a collective activity across the green and blue setting. Compare *Dance*, its companion painting: togetherness need not take the form of continuous touch. Here distinct poses and instruments keep the participants individually legible within an equally reduced pictorial world.

works.title: Madonna Litta
works.credit: Leonardo da Vinci. Madonna Litta (Madonna and the Child). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Mary's lowered head and the child's body form a close group before two openings onto distant blue. The Hermitage presents the painting as Leonardo's, while other scholarship assigns a larger role to his workshop; the attribution remains disputed. The nursing relationship is organised through joined contours and a clear separation from the landscape beyond.

works.title: The Conestabile Madonna
works.credit: Raphael. The Madonna Conestabile. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The child's reach towards the book gives the pair a shared object of attention. Raphael fits that small action inside a circular field without making the bodies rigidly symmetrical. Curves connect the figures to the boundary, while the landscape continues around them. The format shapes the composition all the way from its outer edge to the child's reaching hand.

works.title: Madonna and Child before a Fireplace
works.catalogueTitle: Madonna and Child Before a Fireplace
works.credit: Robert Campin. Madonna and Child Before a Fireplace. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/robert-campin/madonna-and-child-before-a-fireplace-1430
works.description: The fire, window and small fittings establish a room that could support ordinary daily activity. Campin places the sacred pair within those material particulars while keeping their close relationship distinct. The household setting does not have to become mere background symbolism. Its furnishings also make the space usable, bringing the devotional encounter into a comprehensible interior.

works.title: Place de la Concorde
works.credit: Edgar Degas. Place de la Concorde. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Bodies cross near the edge of a broad square, and the frame cuts some of them abruptly. Degas refuses the stable enclosure expected of a conventional family group. The man's, girls' and dog's unequal positions make the encounter feel contingent. Public space continues around them instead of being arranged solely to contain their relationship.

works.title: Blue Landscape
works.credit: Blue Landscape. WikiArt; Paul Cézanne. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Blue and violet foliage gathers around a lighter opening, with buildings and terrain only partly resolved. Relationships among colour patches make Cézanne's landscape readable even where outlines fall away. The eye has to decide where one mass ends and another distance begins. Surface and depicted space remain visible as competing but connected organisations.

works.title: A Group of Cottages
works.credit: A Group of Cottages. WikiArt; Vincent van Gogh. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Strokes change direction as they pass from roofs to walls and foreground field. Van Gogh makes the clustered houses structurally distinct while keeping the whole surface active. Each material receives its own pattern of marks. The village therefore holds together through brushwork whose visible differences also explain the forms it builds.

works.title: Landscape with a House and Ploughman
works.credit: Vincent van Gogh. Landscape with House and Ploughman. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The small worker gives the cultivated slopes a human measure without becoming their visual centre. Yellow and red bands carry attention across land shaped by agricultural use. Van Gogh makes labour part of the landscape's larger organisation. The ploughman matters partly because the ground extends so far beyond the body occupied with working it.

works.title: Breakfast
works.credit: Diego Velázquez. Breakfast. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/diego-velazquez/breakfast
works.description: The raised vessel links a standing figure to the two men at the table. Velázquez gives bread, containers and cloth a role in serving and eating. Gestures turn the meal into a coordinated activity. The objects explain what the group can do together within a closely bounded space, carrying attention between the standing body and the seated pair.

works.title: David and Uriah
works.credit: David and Uriah. WikiArt; Rembrandt van Rijn. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: One richly dressed figure receives light while another remains less available in shadow. The hand against the chest makes a restrained gesture carry substantial attention. Rembrandt supplies a tense encounter without showing every stage of the named story. The unequal visibility is worth retaining as a question rather than filling it with a confident account of each participant's thoughts.

works.title: Family Portrait
works.credit: Family Portrait. WikiArt; Anthony van Dyck. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The adults lean towards the child, giving family connection a physical shape. Van Dyck varies the heights of the heads and the direction of their attention. Pale hands and collars clarify the contact within dark clothing. The different expressions remain readable within the group, whose coherence comes from these inclinations and points of contact.

works.title: Baroness Anna Stroganova and Her Son Sergey
works.catalogueTitle: Baroness Anna Sergeevna Stroganova and Her Son Sergey
works.credit: Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun. Baroness Anna Sergeevna Stroganova and Her Son Sergey. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/louise-elisabeth-vigee-le-brun/baroness-anna-sergeevna-stroganova-and-her-son-sergey-1793
works.description: The child's outward look opens the mother's embrace towards the viewer. Vigée Le Brun keeps the pair physically close while permitting that second direction of attention. Warm clothing separates them from the darker landscape, making an intimate act part of a social portrait. The image stages affection without requiring it to explain every aspect of the sitters' relationship.

works.title: House in a Garden
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. House in a Garden. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/house-in-a-garden-1908
works.description: Walls, roofs and tree forms interlock within a compressed space. Picasso leaves enough architectural information for a house to remain recognisable while making its boundaries cooperate with the vegetation around it. The garden no longer serves as a loose setting for a separate building. Both participate in the same organisation of angular masses across the surface.

works.title: Zorah Standing
works.credit: Henri Matisse. Zorah Standing. Image credit: Henri Matisse. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The narrow frontal figure occupies most of the vertical field, with hands gathered near the waist. Matisse makes the silhouette and repeated ornament carry a strong relationship between body and garment. In the monochrome reproduction used here, those patterns remain readable; the painting's colour relationships do not. It is better to preserve that limit than describe hues the image cannot show.

works.title: Dishes and Fruit
works.credit: Henri Matisse. Dishes and Fruit. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Some objects tilt towards the viewer instead of submitting to one stable tabletop perspective. Matisse uses that adjustment to keep dishes, fruit and patterned cloth active together. Their relationships depend on colour and repeated shapes as well as depth. The still life can be coherent without pretending that every object has been seen from exactly the same position.

works.title: Madonna and Child in a Landscape
works.catalogueTitle: Madonna and Child in a Landscape
works.credit: Madonna and Child in a Landscape. WikiArt; Giorgione. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The red and green clothing anchors the close pair before a landscape of rock, buildings and distant mountains. In this work associated with Giorgione, the terrain has a reach and complexity of its own beyond the devotional group. The contrast of scales matters: a small act of support belongs within a world whose extent does not depend on it.

works.title: Bathing
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Bathing. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/bathing-1908
works.description: Broad curves and sharp joints give the two bodies a recognisable activity while changing the anatomy through which it is shown. Picasso leaves little open interval around them, so surrounding forms remain closely involved. The scene does not provide a smoothly continuous place. Bodily recognition persists through the turns and actions even where conventional spatial reassurance has been withdrawn.

closingSections.title: Compare contact and distance
paragraphs: Return to *Dance* after a family portrait and compare what a handclasp or embrace actually connects. Similar gestures can serve quite different pictures. The Hermitage's holdings occupy more than one building and works may move; use current museum information to establish location and display rather than treating this selection as a single-room itinerary.
